subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What framework-level plugin circuit breaker contract should OpenClaw support for plugin hooks/tools, persisted state, operator controls, and default degradation behavior?
rationale: Current main has partial timeouts and plugin-local breaker precedent, but choosing fail modes, forced-open behavior, status/reset surfaces, storage schema, default-on policy, and third-party plugin API shape is a product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
options.body: Define attribution, SQLite state, hook/tool skip semantics, metrics/status/reset surfaces, per-plugin degradation policy, and passive-to-active rollout before implementation.

options.title: Keep Breakers Plugin-Owned
options.body: Continue adding targeted plugin-local breakers and extract only narrow SDK helpers after multiple plugins need the same mechanism.

options.title: Start With Passive Telemetry
options.body: Add plugin/hook timing and lock attribution plus log-only breaker evaluation, then decide active open/half-open behavior from real deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design Core Breaker Contract First
recommendation.body: Define attribution, SQLite state, hook/tool skip semantics, metrics/status/reset surfaces, per-plugin degradation policy, and passive-to-active rollout before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current history signal across the hook runner, plugin tool runtime, and adjacent plugin-runtime refactors.
